unit.why: The Maggid of Kozhnitz tells a short legend explaining the Raavad's gloss on Maimonides: when Maimonides stated the halakhah, darkness fell in the upper world and souls were driven from Paradise, until the Raavad rejected the ruling and they returned. The events concern pre-Hasidic sages and it sits inside an exegetical frame.

stories.summary_en: The Maggid of Kozhnitz explains that Maimonides' ruling calling believers in a corporeal God heretics caused darkness in the upper world and drove multitudes of souls from Paradise; the Raavad saw this, rejected the ruling, and the souls returned to Paradise.

tags.why: A legend about the Raavad and Maimonides, figures outside the Hasidic movement, showing the Raavad's heavenly perception and power.
The tale is an exegetical explanation of the Raavad's gloss on Hilkhot Teshuvah.

quotes: חמשה נקראים מינים האומר שיש רבון אחד
tags.why: A halakhic ruling of Maimonides and its rejection by the Raavad are the subject.
The action unfolds in the upper world and Gan Eden.

quotes: וכאשר ראה הראב"ד ז"ל שנתהווה חושך גדול
tags.why: The Raavad perceives events in the upper world.
The fate of souls in the afterlife is at stake.
The Maggid of Kozhnitz is the teller of the legend.
